mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority of country of origin (e.g., Chinese National Immigration Administration for PRC shareholders)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association of foreign corporate shareholders (if any direct corporate UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / excerpt of criminal record for each proposed director and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Federal Office of Police (fedpol) or equivalent foreign competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the deposit of minimum share capital (CHF 100,000)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Swiss or foreign commercial bank maintaining the applicant relationship

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Swiss incorporating attorney/licensed fiduciary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public or foreign notary with apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and ultimate beneficial controllers against the UN Security Council sanctions list, OFAC SDN List, Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) sanctions registers, EU consolidated sanctions lists, and FINMA enforcement lists. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified under Art. 2(a) AMLA and require enhanced due diligence with documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence. Negative screening results must be archived and made available to MROS (Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland) and FINMA on demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) in Latin script; transliteration of foreign marks is accepted when rendered in the chosen official language. The name must comply with the principle of veracity (Art. 950 CO) and must not mislead the public as to the company's purpose or legal form. A company name may be in a foreign language only with a clear Swiss element and prior register confirmation; the mandatory legal form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' must be included.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: International Chamber of Commerce / state monopolies
Terms indicating public authority or state sponsorship
Names identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Cantonal Commercial Register Office rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative objection (Einsprache) with the same register office within 30 days stating grounds of rebuttal, followed by an appeal to the cantonal administrative or civil supervisory authority (government council of the canton), and finally to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) in Lausanne; the corrected name may be re-filed with a new preliminary confirmation without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A pure virtual office without physical presence in the registered municipality is not generally acceptable for an AG; Swiss commercial register practice requires a genuine physical registered office address (registered in the canton of seat) where legal notices can be served. A physical office-sharing or commercial representation address is acceptable if contractual rights to use the premises are evidenced; the industry (vertical micro-drama streaming) being non-licensed and low risk permits a light physical footprint, but not a nominal-only address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% - Low to medium probability for a low-risk standard entity; cantonal authorities and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) may conduct unannounced on-site inspections if anomalies appear in the commercial register filing, UBO data, or in the event of a suspicious activity report; the likelihood rises to 50%+ if the company uses an offshore-connected UBO chain or inconsistent nominee structures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des Obligations), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), as revised by the Swiss Company Law Reform of 19 June 2020, in force since 1 January 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA), Federal Department of Justice and Police, Berne.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung im Handelsregister) founded on a notarised deed of incorporation (öffentlich beurkundeter Gründungsakt).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000. At least CHF 50,000 (20% of nominal capital) must be fully paid-up in cash and deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) with a Swiss bank; the bank's written confirmation of the blocked payment must be submitted to the Commercial Register before registration. Contributions in kind are permitted subject to a special audit report under Articles 628-631 CO.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING BOARD OF [COMPANY NAME] AG At the constitutive meeting held in Zug on [date], the board of directors unanimously resolved: (1) that the deed of incorporation executed before the Cantonal Notary is approved and adopted in full; (2) that the entire share capital of CHF 100,000, consisting of 100 registered par-value shares of CHF 1,000 each, is hereby subscribed, allotted, and issued against the confirmed escrow funds; (3) that the company's registered office is fixed at the address stated in the deed; (4) that [Name] is appointed Chairperson and [Name] is appointed Secretary, each with sole signature authority; (5) that the officers are authorised to file the Commercial Register application, obtain the UID number, and arrange the official gazette publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of the Canton of Zug (öffentliches Notariat)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders appear before the Cantonal Notary to certify the deed of incorporation and the articles of association (Statuten). The deed must state the share capital, share denominations, board composition, place of registered office, and the subscription of all shares. The articles must include any permitted audit waiver in accordance with Art. 727a CO. The founders sign the notarial records; a certified copy is then reserved for the Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Notarial drafting instructions
Articles of association (Statuten) draft
Passport or identity card of each founding shareholder
Power of attorney for representatives of legal person shareholders
Declaration of the source of funds for AML verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies missing mandatory clauses under Art. 626 CO, the record is completed by a supplementary notarial act on the same working day; no new notarisation cycle is required beyond the corrective signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of the Minimum Paid-Up Capital into a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank selected in the Canton of Zug or another Swiss financial centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders open a bank account in the name of the company in formation and transfer the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000. The funds must be declared as paid into the blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) and remain frozen until the Commercial Register entry is completed. The bank issues the formal escrow confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) for attachment to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Company bank account opening form
Certified copy of the notarised deed and articles
Identification documents and beneficial ownership declarations for KYC
Written escrow instruction addressed to the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds or beneficial ownership, the founders file additional source-of-wealth documentation; alternatively, a substitute licensed bank can be appointed without amending the public deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution of the Board of Directors and Statutory Auditor Decision
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding Board of Directors of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders elect one to three natural persons as members of the board of directors. The board determines its signature regime (sole or joint) and decides whether the company qualifies for the audit exemption. The acceptance declarations and specimen signatures are formalised in the first board minutes and are forwarded to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes with resolutions and signatory powers
Acceptance declarations of each director
Specimen signature cards
Resolution on audit waiver or appointment of the statutory auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is disqualified under legal or professional standards, the disqualification must be cured by a replacement resolution and revised specimen signatures; subsequent filing is made on the same application cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Issuance of the Company Identification Number (UID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorised signatories submit the application for entry in the Commercial Register electronically through the Swiss e-Register portal. The application is accompanied by the notarised deed, the bank escrow confirmation, the list of directors, specimen signatures, and acceptance declarations. Upon the completeness review, the registry issues the registered company identity and the federal business identification number (UID).
required_dossiers: Anmeldung zur Eintragung (signed registration form)
Notarised deed of incorporation and articles
Bank confirmation of the CHF 50,000 escrow payment
List of directors and authorised signatories with specimen signatures
Acceptance declarations of directors and auditor
Proof of registered office address consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a formal query (Monition/Verfügung), the notary and signatories file clarifications within the statutory 10-day period; failure to respond leads to refusal, and a fresh application may be submitted with payment of the fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register transmits the new entity entry to the SHAB for mandatory publication. The notice includes the company name, legal form, legal seat, purpose, share capital, and the powers of the registered persons. The publication completes the incorporation procedure and creates legal effect vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: Authenticated extract of the entry in the Commercial Register
Registry notification of the completed incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Material errors in the published notice are corrected at the written request of the company to the Commercial Register Office, which submits a rectified notice to the SHAB at the company's cost.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no physical industrial establishment. Advisory reference: Federal Office of Culture (Bundesamt für Kultur, BAK), Films Section, for the optional registration of the film support levy under the Swiss Film Act (Bundesgesetz über das Filmwesen).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory media or broadcasting licence is required in Switzerland for the digital distribution of vertical micro-dramas as video-on-demand. Under Art. 12 of the Film Act, a payment-based VOD provider whose Swiss turnover exceeds the statutory threshold must register with the Federal Office of Culture solely for the levy obligation, which does not condition the lawful start of operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA requirement. The undertaking is a purely digital content production and distribution enterprise with no physical manufacturing site; it does not fall within the mandatory screening lists of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharge obligations arise. The company must, however, dispose of computing hardware and studio batteries in accordance with the Swiss Ordinance on the Avoidance and Disposal of Waste (VVEA) and the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV); the use of cloud infrastructure should ensure supplier compliance with the Ordinance on Green Economy principles where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: the studio and office premises in Zug must obtain the fire safety certificate of the Cantonal Fire Prevention Authority in accordance with the Zug fire protection regulations (VVZ), including structural load inspections. Occupational clearance: the workplace must satisfy the workplace safety review under Art. 82 of the Swiss Labour Act, supervised by the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA), covering first-aid equipment, ergonomic workstations, and the fire evacuation plan prior to staff deployment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer, Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; portal: www.esty.admin.ch and https://estvplus.admin.ch (eServices). For Zug: Kantonales Steueramt Zug, Industriestrasse 26, 6301 Zug; portal: www.zg.ch/steuern.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Incorporation of the AG: notarial deed with entry in the Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug. Step 2 – Automatic issuance of the Swiss Business Identification Number (UID, Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, Format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX) via the central register (Zefix). Step 3 – VAT registration: the AG must register with the ESTV within 30 days after the statutory condition is met (worldwide taxable turnover exceeding CHF 100,000 p.a.) using the ESTV registration form/eServices, effective from the beginning of the month in which the obligation arises. Step 4 – A foreign entity with no Swiss seat must appoint a VAT representative domiciled in Switzerland (Art. 67 para 2 LTVA) unless the ESTV waives the requirement; the representative files on behalf of the foreign principal. Step 5 – Income tax registration: the Commercial Register automatically notifies the Zug Cantonal Tax Office; the AG files annual corporate tax returns (Form B) for federal, cantonal and communal profit/capital taxes; provisional quarterly prepayments are set by the tax office. Foreign shareholders need no separate Swiss tax ID for the AG, but receive a specific shareholder identification number for withholding tax/quotas where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Aktiengesellschaft is a capital company (Kapitalgesellschaft) subject to Swiss federal corporate income tax (Impôt fédéral direct, Art. 49 ff. DBG) at 8.5% of net taxable profit (approximately 7.83% effective after deduction of the tax itself) plus canton/commune corporate taxes in Zug (combined Zug effective total approx. 14.6% in 2025), plus annual capital tax at the cantonal level. The AG is not a pass-through entity; dividends paid to shareholders are subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax (reduced by treaty). Switzerland taxes resident companies on worldwide income, with foreign permanent establishments and real estate exempted via allocation (subject to progression) and participation deduction for qualifying dividends/capital gains.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box exists under Swiss law; the AG is per se an entity-level taxpayer. Available elections and regimes: (1) VAT group (Mehrwertsteuergruppe, Art. 21 LTVA) – related entities may form a single VAT unit via an election filed with the ESTV. (2) Participation deduction (Art. 70 DBG) – eligible dividends and capital gains on qualifying participations (≥10% or fair market value ≥CHF 1 million) are deducted; application in the tax return is mandatory once conditions are met. (3) STAF tax regimes: election of the patent box (Art. 24b DBG and cantonal rules) giving a preferential tax base on IP income, and election of the R&D super-deduction of 50% (Art. 25a DBG) – both require prior cantonal approval. (4) Hybrid mismatch avoidance: Swiss law denies deductions for payments that are not taxable for the recipient under BEPS Action 2; there is no election to re-characterize hybrid instruments except via structuring and documentation in the tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT – Mehrwertsteuer MWST / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée TVA), governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (LTVA, SR 641.20) and its Ordinance (SR 641.201).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) from supplies of goods and services (Art. 10 para 2 let a LTVA); non-profit organizations, public entities and certain charitable businesses use a CHF 250,000 threshold (Art. 10 para 2 let b LTVA). A foreign digital service supplier supplying Swiss private consumers (B2C) is registrable at the same CHF 100,000 worldwide threshold under the simplified foreign supplier procedure, without entitlement to input VAT deduction. A Swiss-resident AG distributing micro-dramas through a streaming app must register once subscriptions, licensing and advertising revenues exceed CHF 100,000. Reduced rates apply: 2.6% for food, press, pharmaceuticals and books and 3.7% for accommodation services; the 8.1% standard rate applies to digital streaming subscriptions and licensing fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API data transmission or digital stamping regime as of 2025. The ESTV accepts paper, PDF or EDI invoices if the data of Art. 26 LTVA are present (supplier/recipient name and address, supplier VAT ID, date, nature of supply, amount, applicable VAT rate). Since 30 June 2020, all invoices intended for payment in Switzerland must include the Swiss QR-code (QR-Rechnung); however, QR-payment slips are a payment facilitation instrument, not a fiscal control mechanism. Business-to-business e-invoicing (eBill, EDI/XML) operates on private standards, and the Federal Council has announced possible mandatory e-invoicing for B2B after 2026, but no final law is in force for the current period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating under Swiss VAT arises in two forms: (A) Export of goods (Art. 23 para 1 LTVA) – not applicable to the core micro-drama business as there is no physical movement of goods; applicable only to ancillary export of hardware/servers. (B) Services with the place of supply outside Switzerland, i.e. 'export of services' (Art. 23 para 2 LTVA). For the streaming app: subscriptions sold to private consumers resident abroad are not subject to Swiss VAT because electronically supplied services to consumers are located in the consumer's country of residence; global licensing of micro-drama copyrights and production output to foreign commissioning platforms (B2B) is zero-rated when the recipient's place of business is abroad. The Swiss supplier retains the full input VAT deduction linked to such exported supplies. Subscriptions by Swiss consumers are taxable at 8.1%. Documentary proof of the foreign place of supply (Art. 45–46 LTVA) must be kept by the supplier, including evidence of the customer's domicile or business seat (e.g. foreign VAT number, commercial register extract, bank/card billing country, IP/geo-location logs and app-store settlement statements from Apple, Google and Stripe).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / déclaration d'exportation) lodged electronically in the Swiss customs system 'Passar' – required only for physical exports in the content-production supply chain (e.g. filming equipment, hardware, promotional materials shipped abroad)
Transport document evidencing international movement: Bill of Lading (seafreight) / Air Waybill (airfreight) / CMR (road) – only where physical goods are exported

Commercial invoice and service agreement with the foreign customer, including the exact description of the licensed micro-drama catalogue or streaming subscription and the foreign place-of-supply indicators
Payment evidence: bank/credit-card settlement records, Stripe or Apple/Google app-store remittance reports proving execution and FX (or stablecoin) inflow from the foreign counterparty
For financing an invoice, an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a Swiss statutory document; Swiss banks issue payment confirmations that serve as the practical substitute
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss law does not set a specific statutory deadline for repatriation of export proceeds; the 180-day benchmark is the documentary best-practice window applied by tax auditors to verify that export proceeds were actually received. During a VAT audit (Art. 78 ff. LTVA), the burden of proof of the export/foreign place of supply lies with the supplier; missing evidence triggers a corrective assessment (Nachbelastung) plus late-payment interest (3.5% p.a. in 2025). Negligent or intentional false zero-rating constitutes VAT evasion (Art. 96 LTVA) with penalties from 1x to 3x the tax evaded; deliberate tax fraud (Art. 97 LTVA) is a criminal offence punishable by fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. The VAT assessment limitation period is 10 years, and is unlimited in the case of fraud (Art. 99 LTVA); in practice the ESTV may also claw back wrongly deducted input VAT retroactively for 10 years and publish decisions on wilful offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), acting under the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank and the Foreign Exchange Ordinance; the State Secretariat for International Financial Affairs (SIF) also coordinates international financial-market policy in this domain.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible. Switzerland is bound by the IMF Article VIII obligations and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Current Invisible Operations and Capital Movements. Both current account payments and capital transfers are unrestricted; no exchange-control authorization is required for capital injection, dividend distribution, or the opening of foreign-currency accounts. The main profit-remittance hurdle is the 35% federal withholding tax on dividends and certain interest payments, which is reduced or eliminated under an applicable double-taxation treaty. A Swiss AG may distribute only net retained statutory profit; any distribution from hidden reserves must be properly documented to avoid tax recharacterization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds under Swiss law. Foreign-currency export receipts may be retained in the original currency without limit, and no obligation arises to convert them into Swiss francs. The only requirements are commercial bookkeeping and tax-transparency rules, accurate custody of underlying invoices, and the normal bank AML due-diligence obligation to identify the economic purpose and source of funds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. An offshore EMI (e-money institution licensed outside Switzerland) may be used as an app-store collection or payout aggregator, but it cannot serve as the primary treasury bank. A FINMA-licensed Swiss bank remains mandatory for lawful custody of corporate funds, access to Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC), and issuance of a proper CHF/EUR treasury account. Legal constraints: an EMI is not a bank under the Swiss Banking Act, cannot hold client monies as a Swiss bank would, and has no direct access to SIC or euroSIC. Any use of an EMI must be structured strictly as an agent/technical payment provider with full reconciliation and an evidentiary paper trail for the underlying vertical-drama subscription transactions. The feasibility is higher for payment collection from Apple IAP/Google Play than for concentration of corporate treasury balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorized signatory, all directors, and all ultimate beneficial owners is generally required during the initial corporate onboarding. Remote onboarding is available only where the bank has a FINMA-compliant video-identification process for individuals and where all corporate documents are notarized, apostilled, and presented with the original certified extract from the Swiss commercial register. In practice, tier-1 Swiss banks require an in-person interview at the domicile branch for corporate entities, or a notarial deed of attorney granted to a Swiss representative. The standard dossier includes Handelsregister excerpt, articles of incorporation, beneficial-ownership declaration, board resolution on signatory rights, and source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or UBOs with no prior Swiss banking nexus, creating elevated source-of-wealth uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and proof of Tax Identification Number; curriculum vitae; personal and corporate tax residence proofs; audited financial statements of all UBOs; notarized source-of-wealth declaration; detailed business plan for the Swiss AG's vertical-drama streaming and production activities; commercial-register excerpt and trust/constitutive documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border collection through digital distribution channels (Apple IAP, Google Play, Stripe) interpreted as fragmented pooling third-party payments, a common money-laundering red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of executed distribution and commissioning agreements; app-store dashboard settlement reports; monthly payout statements from Apple, Google, and Stripe; the ISIC 5911 business-description narrative; consolidated bank-incoming wire statements matched to user-subscription records; audited or management revenue reconciliation; evidence that each app-store payout corresponds to identifiable sales of the Swiss AG.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Distribution footprint involving sanctioned territories or jurisdictions with high AML/CFT risk, raising prohibition and financial-crime concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geoblocking and territories-restriction policy; updated sanctions and watchlist screening logs; end-user terms identifying blocked countries; current list of active storefronts and licensed territories; compliance certification from the platform operator; internal escalation and adverse-media check records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party royalty or production-payment flows to low-tax or offshore entities, creating undisclosed-beneficial-ownership and transfer-mispricing risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group chart incorporating each legal entity and its tax residence; OECD transfer-pricing documentation covering the vertical-drama IP-licensing fee; comparative royalty-rate benchmark studies; board minutes approving royalty terms; certificate of good standing and tax-residence certificate for each payee; evidence of real operational substance of the receiving entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The founding shareholder or institutional investor wires the subscription price via SWIFT MT103 (or SIC for CHF-denominated domestic payments). The payment instruction and reference field must identify the transaction as a capital contribution to the Swiss AG, referencing the share-subscription agreement, the notarized deed of incorporation, and the relevant provision of the Swiss Code of Obligations. The receiving Swiss bank verifies the remitter's identity, confirms the value date, and matches the funds to the commercial-register entry and board resolution on share issuance. For cross-border EUR or USD flows, the regional correspondent bank will validate the MT103 against OFAC/EU/CH sanctions lists and the beneficiary name in the exact commercial-register denomination. No Swiss exchange-control approval is required; however, the bank may require the statutory balance-of-payments statistical declaration to be completed by the corporate client where cross-border direct investment thresholds apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements and production disbursements use Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) for CHF payments, euroSIC and TARGET2 for EUR payments, and SWIFT MT103 for non-CHF cross-border transfers. SWIFT MT202 is reserved for bank-to-bank payments and liquidity movements. Commercial documentary letters of credit are issued in accordance with UCP 600 using SWIFT MT700/MT710 and may cover advance production deposits, license-fee guarantees, and minimum-guarantee obligations. Standby letters of credit and documentary collections may be used to secure royalty receivables from foreign distribution partners. The treasury function must maintain full audit evidence of each payment's purpose, underlying contract, invoice, sanctions screening, and VAT/customs declaration where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain vanilla, up to 24 months, backed by demonstrable production or subscription cash-flow exposure)
FX Swaps (rollover and short-term conversion of foreign-currency revenue into CHF)
Cross-Currency Swaps (including principal exchange, for financing or license obligations)
Foreign Currency Options (call/put structures on projected app-store payouts and production costs)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies, permissible when the underlying non-CHF exposure is verified by actual or contracted receivables/payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) and adoption thereof at the annual general meeting (Generalversammlung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the Swiss corporation under CO art. 698; the board of directors (Verwaltungsrat) prepares the accounts and convenes the meeting; signed accounts and minutes retained at the registered office in the Canton of Zug
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the business year (calendar-year AG: by 30 June) under CO art. 699 para. 2
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off for late AGM in Switzerland; board members incur civil liability under CO art. 754 for damage caused by delayed or inaccurate accounts; missing or defective bookkeeping also triggers tax- and commercial-register fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent auditor's report (Revisionsbericht) presented to the annual general meeting; deposit of annual accounts with the commercial register for larger companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss statutory auditor and the Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (deposit only for AGs exceeding the filing thresholds under CO art. 959f)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report to the board prior to the AGM, in all cases within 6 months after year-end; deposit for qualifying larger AGs within 12 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to deliver the report exposes board members to civil liability and, in liquidation or court proceedings, to judicial measures under CO art. 731b; failure of a qualifying larger AG to deposit accounts can trigger administrative penalties under commercial-register ordinances (fines up to CHF 5,000).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income-tax return covering federal direct tax, Zug cantonal tax and municipal tax, including capital-tax schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Steuerverwaltung des Kantons Zug (cantonal and municipal tax) and Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) for federal direct tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the business year end (calendar-year AG by 30 June); extension to 30 September or later is granted upon written application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder charges; default interest (Verzugszins) at 4% p.a. on Federal tax under DBG art. 129; discretionary estimated assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) where books are not produced; administrative fine of up to CHF 10,000 under DBG art. 175 for culpable failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT (MWST/IVA) periodic returns and payment of assessed VAT on streaming-app revenues
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT division, via the e-filing portal (Münzgasse / Swiss Federal e-VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Turnover-dependent periods: semi-annual or quarterly returns; return and payment due within 60 days after the end of each period (90 days for semi-annual periods) under VAT Act art. 86
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment reminders; statutory default interest at 4.5% p.a. under MWSTG art. 87; fines up to CHF 8,000 for ordinary violations and up to CHF 23,000 for intentional tax evasion under MWSTG art. 94-95.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer payroll declaration and settlement of old-age, disability, unemployment and allocation contributions (AHV/IV/EO/ALV) plus UVG occupational-accident insurance reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ausgleichskasse (Swiss compensation fund) competent for the AG's registered seat and the SUVA or private accident-insurance carrier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer annual wage declaration within 60 days after the end of the calendar year (end February); contribution payments due on payroll dates with a final balancing payment at year-end settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a. on unpaid social-insurance contributions; administrative fines for under-declared salaries; proceedings for willful non-payment can lead to criminal sanctions under AHVG and related enforcement by the compensation fund.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) statutory audit is mandatory when, for two consecutive years, two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, or more than 250 full-time employees (CO art. 727). All other AGs require only a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) unless, with unanimous shareholder consent, the AG validly opts out of any audit when it does not exceed 10 full-time employees on annual average (CO art. 727a para. 2 and 727b).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (CO art. 957-963g, 'Swiss GAAP OR/CO'); IFRS and Swiss GAAP FER are permitted as recognized standards; the statutory annual accounts are presented in CHF, with disclosure if the reporting currency differs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AMLA art. 4, the AG must maintain an internal, current record of beneficial owners (wirtschaftlich Berechtigte) available to the tax and supervisory authorities on request; each share transfer is recorded in the Aktienbuch and the board re-verifies beneficial-ownership details at the time of transfer. Switzerland has no public UBO register and currently no annual UBO confirmation filing with the commercial register. When the federal transparency register for legal entities (Bundesgesetz über die Transparenz juristischer Personen) becomes operational, an initial registration and subsequent updates or annual confirmations will be required. Supporting AML/UBO files must be retained for 10 years after the end of the business relationship.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of authorised signatories and registered-office documents
Minute book of shareholders' and board meetings
Annual accounts, audit files and 10-year archive of business correspondence and vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600-3,000 per year for commercial domiciliation, registered-office address and statutory correspondence-forwarding services in the Canton of Zug (typical Zug corporate-services market range).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if a valid audit opt-out is in force (unanimous shareholder waiver and no more than 10 FTE); approximately USD 3,000-9,000 per year for a limited audit; approximately USD 20,000-60,000 per year for a full statutory audit.
